YOM(1) YOM User Manual YOM(1)

NAME

yom - lightweight, non-interactive micro-shell and systems glue

SYNOPSIS

yom [SCRIPT_FILE]

DESCRIPTION

yom is a lightweight, high-performance micro-shell and systems glue utility written in Rust. Developed as a memory-safe alternative to dash, it provides efficient scripting execution while avoiding the compilation dependencies associated with traditional C-based shells.

When invoked with a SCRIPT_FILE, yom parses and executes the contained commands sequentially. If no arguments are provided, the utility terminates silently with exit code 0.

Because yom compiles into a single, static binary, it is suitable for deployment as a drop-in execution processor (within limits) in minimal Unix environments, containers, and custom initramfs images.

SYNTAX

yom employs a POSIX-inspired syntax style. To execute a command synchronously and wait for its completion, specify the absolute path:

/bin/program

To execute a command asynchronously in the background, append an ampersand:

/bin/program &

To replace the current shell process image with the target program, use the exec builtin:

exec /bin/program

yom implements the following standard shell builtins:

echo [text]
Prints text to standard output.
read [prompt]
Displays a prompt and reads input from standard input.
cd [path]
Changes the current working directory.
exit [code]
Terminates the shell process with the specified status code.
pwd
Prints the absolute path of the current working directory.
export [name=value]
Sets an environment variable for child processes and subsequent executions.

Environment variables are referenced by prefixing the variable name with a dollar sign ($):

export ls=/bin/ls
$ls
$ls &
exec $ls

The set builtin modifies shell execution options. Use a minus sign (-) to enable an option and a plus sign (+) to disable it:

set -e
Enables immediate termination if a command exits with a non-zero status. 
set +e
Disables immediate termination on command failure.

Additionally, yom includes a non-POSIX builtin named hook, which redirects standard builtins to external binaries or extends shell functionality:

hook <hooked> </path/to/hook/>
For comprehensive details, refer to the yom-hooks(3) manual page.

If Statements

Conditional evaluation uses standard POSIX-style syntax:

if [ 1 -eq 1 ]
then


  echo "one is equal to one"
fi

Variables defined via export may also be evaluated within conditional blocks, provided they are prefixed with $ to ensure value comparison rather than literal string comparison.

NOTES

If you want to pass as an argument, surround it in quotes like this:

"&"
then you can run it with as an argument.

Neat Stuff

in yom if you don't surround the operands with quotes and they arn't integers then yom will treat them as strings, pretty cool.
Another neat thing, [ isn't a alias for the test command, it is a bit of syntax to emulate the look of POSIX, so that yom could execute some POSIX scripts.
